scope: Written reconstruction of 121's actual-pure-input closest-product overlap, same-Q high-noise bound, sorted-radius far bridge, and equality handling; not a new input class or independent review.
actual_overlap_and_union: For a normalized pure psi, the maximum m of squared overlap with local product vectors exists by compactness. Let each local majority projector P_i have probability (1+r_i)/2. They commute across sites, so I-product_i P_i <= sum_i(I-P_i), and the actual joint outcome probability is >=1-(1/2)sum_i(1-r_i). This product outcome is one admissible product vector, hence m >= that probability. Thus 1-m <= (1/2)sum_i(1-r_i). The bound remains valid when a local marginal is maximally mixed; choose any of its majority eigenvectors, with no normalization of a zero Bloch vector.
sorted_radius_bridge: For sorted 0<=r1<=r2<=r3<=r4<=1 and L=r1+r2+3r3+3r4, delta=8-L equals (1-r1)+(1-r2)+3(1-r3)+3(1-r4) >= sum_i(1-r_i). Therefore delta>=2(1-m)=2 eta^2, with eta^2=1-m in the actual closest-product gauge. This is one physical psi throughout; it is not a free tuple of locally independently optimized projectors.
same_Q_pauli_bound: For fixed actual rank-three Q, sum over the twelve weight-one expectations of rho times those of Q equals Tr Q sum_i r_i dot sigma_i. Its top-three eigenvalue sum is L: the all-plus sign and flips of the two least radii, including ties. Orthogonal Pauli Parseval gives sum_nonidentity (Tr Q sigma_w)^2=16Tr Q^2-(Tr Q)^2=39 and, for pure rho, the sum of weight>=2 squared expectations is 15-S. For t=1-p in [0,1], Cauchy and t^k<=t^2 for k>=2 give 16Tr QLambda rho<=3+tL+t^2 sqrt(39(15-S)). The global spinflip maps negative shrink to this same fixed-Q statement.
far_strictness: The reference polynomial is 16R3=3+8t+6t^2-t^4. Since t^4<=t^2, the gap is at least t[delta-t(sqrt(39(15-S))-5)]/16. S>=0 gives sqrt(39(15-S))-5<=sqrt(585)-5<20 because 585<625. If eta>=9/40 and t<=1/200, delta>=81/800>1/10>=20t, so the gap is strictly positive for each actual Q when t>0. The tube/far seam eta=9/40 is covered by both proofs; t=0 uniform and eta=0 product are separate.
